label: debut-good-demand
_why: Where does a NEWLY INVENTED good's demand come from? FINDINGS F28 eliminated the only named mechanism (the max_supply_share cap does NOT hand a debut good a share of its need), so the largest block in the ladder - electrics and automotive insolvent from birth - has no candidate explanation. This watches the order book month by month across every good's first appearance in three markets.
_note: SPAN 1836->1910, not ->1905 as first proposed. pm_telephones is gated on tech adio and automobiles on combustion_engine, BOTH era_4 = vanilla 1887-1911, so 1905 gives them only a narrow window and might catch nothing. The run does not depend on them: era_3 techs (1862-1886) put rubber and electricity well inside the span, and ANY good debuting mid-run exhibits the same mechanism - so the batch cannot come back empty. DEMAND-side by design (the user's point: the good may be invented elsewhere), which is why three markets are watched, GBR and USA as plausible first inventors and RUS as a likely importer. ONE metric only: the compact per-good market line (buy/sell/price/imports/exports/production). consumption_breakdown would give the pop-vs-building split but is ~1MB per market per dump and bursts, which is exactly what evicts the series being measured - so channel attribution is a follow-up run once the appearance dates are known.
